releases.notes:
# Channels, custom prompts and server hardening There's so much good stuff in this release and we're really proud of _all_ of it. Read on for more. ## BYO Prompts At last, you can replace the system prompts with…whatever you want. And not just the main agent but prompts for subagents, planning, compaction, session titles and `crush init`: ```bash option prompt coder ~/.config/crush/prompts/coder.md.tpl option prompt summary prompts/summary.md ``` You can set prompt in the global config, override per project in local config, or override the prompt with `--prompt name=path`. For more on prompts, see [the docs](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/blob/main/docs/config/README.md#option-prompt). ## Riding in the Night Crush now ships with a Knight Rider-inspired KITT theme courtesy @cdancy. Rosé Pine Classic, Moon and Dawn are now available, too.

## Nerd out with Nerd Fonts At last, nerd fonts! Support is detected automatically, so they'll never break your terminal, too! Crush now uses their icons, LSP status and Git included. Note that if you're running Crush over SSH you'll need to enable Nerd fonts `option ui nerd-fonts true`. ```bash # Hate nerd fonts? You can turn 'em off, too. option ui nerd-fonts false ``` ## Channels [Channels](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference) are an experimental MCP feature from Claude, now available in Crush thanks to the fine work of @joestump. In short, channels allow MCP servers to push events into your session as they happen. ```bash crush --channels server:webhook --channels server:signal ``` Or turn one on permanently in your `crushrc`: ```bash # crushrc mcp add webhook \ --type http \ --url https://example.com/mcp \ --channel true ``` Crush uses the same protocol as [Claude Channels](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference), so existing channel servers should just work™. ## Server Hardening Client-server mode is now now sturdier than ever. It's now more secure and has a ton of small improvements, correctness fixes, nad bugfixes, especially on Windows. ## And So Much More - Sysadmin mode is no longer one shift+tab past yolo. - Queued prompts show up in the pill the moment you submit them. - The model can use `sudo`, so you can approve with Touch ID. - Content refusals are retried automatically. - Sessions that Claude kept rejecting work again. - Ollama models that can't call tools no longer show up in the model list. - Commands that leave child processes behind no longer hang. - Timers tick together, and running tool timers keep going until the tool replies. - Switching themes no longer re-renders the whole conversation. - Deleting a session keeps your place in the list. - Replayed messages keep their whitespace, and plan cards line up properly. Good luck, Charm XX 🌤️ ## Changelog ### New! * 01780cc0384227b90071a8bbf26559410b748efc: feat(lsp): Automatically use nerd font for LSP status (#4334) (@BrunoKrugel) * # Skill toggles, tool timers and a faster Hyper ⚡ This release was brought to you by our team and our favorite contributors! Long awaited features ahead, read along! ## Toggle skills Skills can now be switched on and off right from the command palette. Broken skills are easy to spot, too! (they're marked with a red × and the reason they failed) ## 🕐 How long is this taking? Every tool call now shows how long it's been running. Now, you'll know whether that test suite is just slow or actually stuck. ## Lighter, faster Hyper ⚡ Requests to Hyper are now compressed with [Brotli](https://brotli.org/) 🥦. That means much smaller uploads on every turn and snappier responses, especially in long sessions. Hyper now also supports [Gzip](https://www.gzip.org/) that other agents could use when Brotli if not viable. Big thanks to @BrunoKrugel for the first 2 awesome features! # Subagents, Sysadmin Mode, and PGP/SSH Prompts This is a big one! Crush can now run a team of subagents, permissions are much more flexible, and you can now do GPG and SSH auth right inside Crush! Read on for more. ## 👩🏼‍🐰‍👩🏽 Subagents At last, subagents. Crush can now spawn a little team of friendly subagents in the background, as well as check on them, send them mid-run follow-ups, stop them, or move them to a different model.

You can watch them work right in the transcript, sidebar and header. Every subagent gets its own name, too, so you always know who's doing what. And, if you refer to them by name, Crush will know which of ’em you’re talking about! ## 🚨 Sysadmin Mode Ever wish Crush could `DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE;`? Now it can, with Sysadmin mode! In fact, in Sysadmin mode, Crush can run any command on your system. Be careful.

Find Sysadmin mode in the command palette (ctrl+p) or toggle through all modes with shift+tab. ## 🙅🏻‍♀️ Safe Commands Of course, Yolo Mode still blocks dangerous commands, but now which commands are dangerous is up to you. * `permissions safe` marks commands safe for yolo * `permissions block` blocks commands completely * `permissions unblock` unblocks restricted commands ```bash # Building is fine permissions safe "go build" "cargo check" # Don't touch my infra please permissions block kubectl terraform # Curl your heart out permissions unblock curl ``` ## 🗝️ PGP and SSH It’s so annoying when you’re using an AI agent and can’t enter an SSH password, activate your Yubikey and enter GPG passwords, eh? Well, with Crush, that annoyance is a thing of the past. No more compromising your security to when usin’ AI! --- There’s tons more stuff in the changelog below, too. This is one of our biggest releases, and we're _so_ grateful for your support! # Hooks, Catwalk v3! A big one! Crush now runs on Catwalk v3, hooks can see every part of a run, and editors that host Crush get a whole new set of tools to feel right at home. ## Hooks, everywhere 🪝 Hooks are no longer just about tools. They can now follow the whole run: sessions, turns, permissions and more! Hooks can now step in after a tool runs, too. Redact secrets from the output before the model sees them, add a note, or stop the turn. If the tool already did something it shouldn't have, your hook can tell the model "you committed without running the tests." ```bash hook add TurnEnd --name "ding" --command 'afplay /System/Library/Sounds/Glass.aiff' ``` You can read more [here](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/tree/main/docs/hooks#readme) ## Client/server mode If you build something that runs Crush inside it, this release is for you: - Host themes: the host app can theme the TUI over the server API, so Crush matches your applications. - Host context: the host can tell Crush what's in view, like open files, and those files appear in completions. - Append to the next prompt: clients can add text the agent reads with the next prompt, without starting a run or cluttering the chat. - Shared viewing: clients can see which session other clients are looking at. - Piped permissions: set `CRUSH_PERMISSIONS_PIPED=1` and the host answers permission prompts, so you aren't asked twice. - `http://` addresses work as an alias for `tcp://` when starting the server. ## Steadier server - `SIGHUP` now reloads the config instead of stopping the server. - Closing the terminal or stopping Crush through a service manager now shuts down gracefully, so work in progress is saved instead of left looking stuck. ## Small overview of [Catwalk v3][catwalk]: Crush now speaks [Catwalk v3][catwalk]. Provider `type` describes the API format a provider uses, not who made it: - `completions`: OpenAI-compatible APIs - `responses`: OpenAI, or anything routed through it - `messages`: Anthropic-compatible APIs Your config is migrated automatically when it loads, so `openai`, `openai-compat` and `anthropic` keep working. No edits needed. The `provider add` and `model add` flags follow along: ```bash crush provider add deepseek \ --type completions \ --base-url "https://api.deepseek.com/v1" \ --api-key "$DEEPSEEK_API_KEY" crush model add deepseek/deepseek-chat --thinking toggleable --max-attachments 5 ``` - `--can-reason` is now `--thinking always|never|toggleable` - `--max-attachments N` is new - Reasoning levels show friendly names in the picker, like "X-High" [catwalk]: https://github.com/charmbracelet/catwalk/releases/tag/v3.0.0 That's all for now! releases.notes:
## Disable mouse support + more Hey, how's your week going? We have a few changes today, including mostly fixes but also a few nice additions. ## Disable mouse support Want to disable mouse support in Crush? Feel lucky because our favorite contributor @timotheosh added just that. With the config below you can achieve that. It's also possible to toggle it via the command palette dialog. `crushrc`: ```bash option ui mouse false ``` `crush.json`: ```json { "options": { "tui": { "mouse": false } } } ``` ## Fixed UX for non-vision models In some cases, Crush were allowing you to attach an image even when the selected model was not vision-capable. The attachment was then being silent dropped in the request. Now, we're properly validating it and showing a message so you know when it's not supported. ## Fixed some models on GitHub Copilot On Copilot some models only works on the `/responses` endpoint: named GPT-6 Astra and the Grok models. ## Fixed some models on OpenCode Zen & Go OpenCode also require some models to use specific endpoints. Not every model support the `/chat/completions` endpoint; some require `/responses` or `/messages`. We fixed this issue for the models OpenCode currently supports. ## Fixed Sentry MCP + others A misconfiguration made it impossible to authenticate with OAuth2 with a few the MCPs, including the [Sentry MCP](https://mcp.sentry.dev/). This is now fixed! ## Fixed potential memory leak @caniko discovered a memory leak, specifically when `discover_models: true` is set. This issue was fixed! To read the technical explanation, see #3162 and #3683. --- See you in the next release!
